parameters.content:
## YouTube Outlier Finder
### How it works
Every Monday at 9am this workflow checks the YouTube channels you list, finds their long-form videos that far outperformed the channel's usual views, and sends you one Telegram message per outlier with an AI explanation of why it likely popped plus three video ideas for your own channel. Videos come from each channel's official RSS feed via the YouTube Channel Scraper actor on Apify, so results cover recent uploads only. Each video is scored against its own channel's median views; a video must beat the multiplier and the minimum-views floor in the config node to qualify. Outliers already sent are remembered, so the same video is never sent twice. On a quiet week with no new outliers, nothing is sent.
### Setup
1. In 'Set your channels & limits', list the channels to watch and describe your own channel.
2. Connect your Apify account in 'Scrape channels on Apify' (runs are billed per video to your Apify account).
3. Connect a Gemini API key in 'Chat model (Gemini)', or swap in another chat model.
4. Put your Telegram chat ID in both Telegram nodes and connect your bot.
### Customization
Raise the multiplier for only the biggest breakouts, lower the view floor for small channels, change the Monday schedule, or edit the LLM prompt to match your niche.

## 🎥 Watch the tutorial
@[youtube](3CgDb_Ymtng)
The full build, step by step — how the finder works, how to set it up, and how to read the alerts.

## ⚠️ Edit the Set node first
The workflow ships with placeholder channels. Until you replace them with real ones, it will find nothing.

## 1 · Start here — your settings
Every knob lives in the Set node: the channels to watch, the outlier multiplier, the minimum-views floor, how many recent videos per channel get scored, and a one-line description of your channel for the AI. Edit it before anything else.

## 2 · Fetch recent videos
The Apify actor reads each channel's official YouTube RSS feed and returns its recent long-form uploads, Shorts excluded. One run covers every channel in your list. If the scrape itself fails, the side branch sends you a failure alert instead of staying silent.

## 3 · Score & dedupe
Each video is compared with its own channel's median views. Only videos beating your multiplier and view floor pass, and any video already sent in an earlier week is dropped. No new outliers means the run ends here and the week stays silent.

## 4 · Explain & alert
The LLM explains why each outlier likely popped and drafts three ideas for your channel. You get one Telegram message per outlier, with its views, ratio and link — never a combined digest.
